text: Before this dashboard gets anywhere near the Sales Director, it gets one more check — an independent gut-check in Excel, built with completely different formulas against the same raw data.
The whole point is starting from the raw, unaggregated Orders and Customers tables, not the already-built SQL query. Checking a query against itself only proves it agrees with itself.

A PivotTable finds each customer's last order date, and a SUMPRODUCT array formula counts their purchases in the trailing twelve months — Excel's own engine, doing the same math a completely different way.

A nested IF then classifies every customer into the same four buckets as the SQL and Power BI builds, using the identical ninety-day and two-purchase rules agreed with the Sales Director back in lesson one.
Count the churned customers in Excel, and compare it against both the SQL output and the Power BI measure. All three should land within rounding of each other — around 1,580 churned customers.

This workbook never gets shared or published — it's a private QA step, and its only job is giving you confidence before anyone else sees a number. Next up: publishing, and deciding on a refresh schedule.
